t: Epochs of Power Research Lands as SnapDog Gets a Slide
s: A paperwork day: my Epochs of Power game research was saved to git, SnapDog got a one-slide story, and Lectern's ads were corrected.

t: Epochs of Power Records Where the Old Game Decides Ties
s: My strategy-game research gained a long set of written findings about Call to Power II, plus scripts that watch the original game run.

t: Grok Bot Notes Record a Quiet Day and a Mac Mini Back Online
s: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded no changes to any bot, and noted that the Mac mini reconnected after a day offline.

t: Hermes Fleet Misses the Same Laptop for a Sixth Morning
s: My house assistant's overnight head-count again could not find one laptop, and my NAS now has less spare memory than at any earlier check.

t: Lectern Gets Ad Copy That Matches What the Store Sells
s: The Mac app itself did not change; I wrote new ad copy after finding my own notes undersold what the store version already does.

t: SnapDog Gets a One-Slide Story of Its Road to the Store
s: The app itself was unchanged, but I added a one-slide summary of how it went from idea to the Mac App Store.

t: Dead Signal's Book Page Gets Tracking and a New Sample Address
s: The Dead Signal pages on my books site now report where visitors came from, and the opening sample has moved to a new address.

t: Dead Signal Gets Ad Tracking as SnapDog Notes Get Fixed
s: Dead Signal's book pages learned to track where ad visitors come from, and my own SnapDog notes turned out to be wrong about its release.

t: Hermes Fleet Misses the Same Laptop for a Fifth Morning
s: My house assistant's overnight head-count again could not reach one laptop, and the spare memory on my NAS fell to its lowest figure so far.

t: Remnant Academy Gets a Tax Switch and a Payment Fix
s: The academy's checkout can now collect sales tax once I switch it on, and a payment-recording check that could hide failures was tightened.

t: SnapDog Gets New Ad Research After Its Own Notes Were Wrong
s: The app did not change, but I wrote new ad copy for SnapDog after finding my own notes still called the shipped app unreleased.

t: SnapDog Gets a First Demo Film as Hermes Fleet Fails
s: SnapDog, my Mac screenshot app, now has a two-minute silent demo film for its website, while my house assistant failed its morning check again.

t: Grok Bot Notes Record Eleven Assistants Renamed in a Day
s: The notes on my fleet of assistants noted that eleven bots were renamed with a new title style, and that no new bots appeared.

t: Hermes Fleet Fails Its Morning Check for a Fourth Day
s: My house assistant's morning health report failed again and its head-count still cannot reach one laptop, but the other three machines answered normally.

t: SnapDog Gets a First Silent Film Cut for Its Website
s: The first complete demo film for SnapDog's website exists as a silent two-minute story, and the notes say plainly which features it does not yet prove.

t: Hermes Fleet Misses a Laptop as Grok Bot Adds Two Bots
s: A quiet Monday: SnapDog's old proof files went into version control, Hermes Fleet lost a laptop again, and Grok Bot's notes caught up.

t: Grok Bot Documents Two New Assistants After a Missed Week
s: The house notes for my fleet of assistants caught up after five days without a refresh and added two new bots, one for election mail and one for phone calls.

t: Hermes Fleet Recounts the House and Still Misses a Laptop
s: My house assistant's overnight head-count still cannot reach one laptop, and its morning health report failed again because the model server stayed silent.

t: SnapDog Files Its Scrolling-Capture Proof and Two Decks
s: The app did not change; I filed the proof that scrolling capture works, my demo-film shoot notes and two slide decks telling its story.

t: Hermes WebUI Went Live and the Fleet Lost Its Voice
s: My house assistant put a web front-end on my private network in eight minutes, while its morning health report failed and its evening voice crashed.

t: Hermes Fleet Loses Its Voice and a Laptop Stays Missing
s: The house assistant's morning health report failed and its evening spoken summary crashed outright, while the overnight head-count still misses one laptop.

t: Hermes WebUI Gives My House Assistant a Screen of Its Own
s: The house assistant installed a browser front-end for itself tonight and had it answering on my phone within eight minutes.

t: Lightfence's Mac Steam Candidate Is Built and Recorded
s: A complete unsigned Mac build of the puzzle game now exists as a Steam candidate, and its build record landed in the repository tonight.

t: SnapDog Stops One Blank Frame From Killing a Recording
s: A Mac screen recording could be ruined by a single empty frame; SnapDog now drops those frames and the recording survives.

t: Epochs of Power Opponent Stops Peeking at Your Units
s: The computer opponent in my strategy prototype no longer sees the whole map, so it now has to scout like a player would.

t: A Fire TV Stick Loses Its Trackers, With an Undo Button
s: I started stripping tracking and advertising services off a streaming stick, with backups and a one-command way to put everything back.

t: My Assistant Now Picks Which Model Does Each Job
s: My assistant can hand a job to a different model depending on the work, from one running on my own desk to a paid cloud one, and the last route took two false starts to get working.

t: Hermes Fleet Notices That One Computer Has Gone Missing
s: My house assistant re-checked which computers it can reach overnight and found one of them no longer answers to its name.

t: Night Chorus TV Version Now Shares One Purchase
s: Night Chorus, the crystal game formerly called Prism Shift, now uses one identity across all its Apple versions, so a single purchase should cover them.

t: Lightfence Stops Crashing When the Sound Fails to Start
s: Lightfence could quit on its own if the phone's audio was busy when a sound played, and that crash is now fixed.

t: AdGenerator Now Feeds on LaunchDeck's Recordings
s: The ad pipeline can now pull its footage straight from LaunchDeck's recordings of the real apps, with no copying files by hand between the two tools.

t: The Build Fleet Learns Windows and Stops Losing Job Receipts
s: The build system that spreads my compiling work across the house added a Windows worker, kept receipts when connections dropped, and showed memory pressure.

t: Epochs of Power Probes Call to Power II Without a Screen
s: My research project toward a touch-first historical strategy game spent the day documenting the 2000 original and probing it automatically without a display.

t: Teaching My Assistant to Survey the House and Read Aloud
s: My assistant can now check which of my computers are awake, work out where each job should run, and speak a spoken summary of long answers as a playable recording.

t: Hermes Fleet Takes Stock of the House and Reads Answers Aloud
s: My house assistant can now survey which computers are awake, and read long answers aloud as recordings that refuse to say anything the written answer did not.

t: Hisense Podcasts Gets a Native Library and Clearer Controls
s: My television's podcasts app now puts private subscriptions beside regular shows, remembers older episodes, and makes its buttons easier to see.

t: Hisense Podcasts Gets a Native Library That Refreshes Itself
s: The Hisense television's podcasts app now keeps one native library of ordinary and paid private shows, reaches older episodes, and refreshes itself on launch.

t: LaunchDeck Learns All Thirty-Three Apps and Films Godot Too
s: My marketing pipeline tool now knows all thirty-three of my apps and games as build-and-film recipes, including games made in the Godot engine.

t: Let Me Retire Publishes One Dream, One Button and No Payments
s: I published a one-page joke site called Let Me Retire: one dream, one million dollars, one button, and a checkout that honestly reports it is not configured.

t: Meshy's 3D Pipeline Gets a Manual and a Real Audit
s: The toolbox that turns text into three-dimensional models got a single manual for every coding assistant, plus an audit that verified what it can really do.

t: Pipe Flow's Website Now Plays Three Boards in the Browser
s: The Pipe Flow website gained a playable three-board demo built from the game's own art and sound, and the game itself gained tests and a Linux build script.

t: Night Chorus Gets a Release Path, and Alerts Reach My Phone
s: One Friday of plumbing: failures now reach my phone, a skipped night cannot hide, and Night Chorus's first release check found four problems in seconds.

t: Night Chorus Builds for Steam and Fails Its Own Release Check
s: Night Chorus, the crystal game formerly called Prism Shift, built a Linux candidate for Steam and wrote itself a release checklist that failed its first run.

t: Lightfence 1.3 Repaints Its Art and Its Site Says Out Now
s: Lightfence's next version repaints every picture in the game at high resolution with shimmering gems, and its website now carries the store badge.

t: SnapDog Rewrites Its Website Films Around Remote Help
s: The Mac app's help menu now opens the SnapDog website, and the site's demo films were re-planned twice to tell one story about helping someone remotely.

t: YOLK SOULS Rewrites Its README to Match the Real Game
s: The hop-and-die adventure game's project card now describes the playable build that exists, not the month-old design it had outgrown.

t: Pipe Flow's Desktop Audit Found Leaks 34 Seconds Early
s: Checking Pipe Flow's desktop port against the phone game found leaks bursting early on 111 of 140 levels, while Lightfence, SnapDog and StatBar also moved.

t: Hisense Podcasts Gains Private Feeds and Remote Navigation
s: The television's podcasts app gained private show feeds, working remote navigation and a Now Playing card on the home screen.

t: Pipe Flow on Desktop Catches Up With the Phone Game
s: The desktop version of Pipe Flow was brought much closer to the phone game in feel, sound, menus and 13 languages.

t: Lightfence Gets a Tabletop Layout for Folding Phones
s: Lightfence gained a tabletop layout for a folding phone, and build 1004 went to App Store review.

t: SnapDog on Linux Captures a Clicked Window Cleanly
s: SnapDog on Linux now captures a clicked window correctly, without leftover tint or menu ghosts in the picture.

t: StatBar 1.7.0 Trims and Slims Phone Simulators
s: StatBar 1.7.0 can now trim and slim the phone simulators on a Mac on its own, freeing memory and disk.

t: Prism Shift Gets Boss Fights and Lightfence a Film Shelf
s: Prism Shift's second version gained countdown pieces and boss fights, Lightfence added a film shelf, SnapDog on Linux learned GIFs, and tests waited for room.

t: The Hisense TV Gets a Podcasts App That Resumes
s: The television now has a podcasts app that keeps playing with the screen off and picks up where you stopped.

t: Prism Shift's Second Version Gets Its Trickiest Pieces
s: The crystal game's second version gained its trickiest pieces, and the tablet layout and saved progress were made safer.

t: Lightfence Story Films Now Open With Each Stage
s: Lightfence's story films now unlock with each stage and can be rewatched, and the version sent for App Store review was updated.

t: SnapDog on Linux Records GIFs and Picks a Webcam
s: The Linux version of SnapDog can now record GIFs and lets you pick which camera appears in recordings.

t: StatBar 1.6.0 Checks Whether a Mac Is Ready to Work
s: StatBar 1.6.0 can now report whether a Mac is ready for heavy work, and it can check every Mac in a household at once.

t: Pipe Flow Learns Windows, Mac and a Handheld Overnight
s: Overnight a phone puzzle game learned to run on Windows, the Mac and a handheld, three other apps moved onto new screens, and the failures stayed on file next to the fixes.

t: A Finished Post Waited All Morning for a Signature
s: A finished post waited all morning for a signature from a computer that was never down, while the apps it writes about kept shipping all weekend.

t: Learning to Sell, Part 1: $1,010 Spent, Two Copies Sold
s: The first entry in a public tracker of whether the assistants that build my apps and books can earn back what they cost, starting from two paid sales, no ad spend and a lot of numbers nobody can see yet.

t: I Turned My Old Proxmox PC Into a Headless AI Box
s: A retired server became an always-on machine for running AI models, and along the way its memory turned out to be quietly changing data, which I did not believe until we tested it.

t: Could Eight Used PS5s Make a 128 GB Local AI Machine?
s: Eight used game consoles add up to 128 GB of fast memory on paper, but locked software and slow network links change the plan, and a cheaper board with the same chip already has people clustering it.

t: Grok Bot Gets Real Docs, Shared Rules and This Public Diary
s: The shop of writing-and-building assistants got real docs, shared tool rules, a tuned coding helper, and this public diary, with nine routing experiments still waiting to run.

t: Week of October 12: Lightfence Gets a Name
s: A game renamed and sent to Apple in thirteen languages, two games on the television, site views up from 19 to 52, no paid sales, and model experiments still waiting to run.

t: Prism Shift's Rising Water Now Fills the Drowned Spaces
s: The crystal game's rising water now fills the drowned spaces properly, and the television version got clearer text and a quieter start.

t: Lightfence Menus Now Read From the Couch on Apple TV
s: Lightfence's menus now read from the couch on Apple TV, and the tutorial teaches the game's pickups and the glowing orb.

t: All Fourteen Remnant Security Web Addresses Now Pass
s: The company's web addresses were checked one by one for search and sharing, and all fourteen now pass, including the new StatBar site.

t: Remnant Academy Becomes Findable by Search Engines
s: The paid training site can now be found by search engines and shows a proper preview card when its pages are shared.

t: Site Templates: A Shared Starter Kit for Product Sites
s: A shared starter kit for the company's product web sites was built, with one layout for apps and one for games.

t: StatBar 1.0 Goes on Sale With One Price for All Macs
s: StatBar went on sale as version 1.0 with one price for unlimited Macs, and it gained a clean-up tool, AI developer views and a lighter memory footprint.

t: A Stubborn Monitor Was Really a Cable Problem
s: A monitor that refused to follow the desk switch to the personal laptop was traced to a cable, and unplugging it fixed it.

t: Prism Shift on Apple TV Starts Reliably and Runs Smoother
s: The Apple TV version of the crystal game now starts reliably on the shed television, steers with the remote's touch ring, and runs smoother.

t: Lightfence Dev Diary: A New Name and 13 Languages
s: In one long day the game became Lightfence, learned twelve more languages, went to Apple for review, gained a tutorial you learn by playing, and its last sectors got fairer.

t: QixForge Becomes Lightfence in 13 Languages
s: The game was renamed Lightfence, translated into 13 languages, and filled in with a tutorial and living scenery before its App Store listing.

t: Remnant Security's Front Page Becomes Search-Readable
s: The company's front page was made readable to search engines and link previews, and two game sites went live under their own addresses.

t: SnapDog's English Demo Video Finally Gets Recorded
s: A 35-second English demo video of SnapDog was finally recorded, after four failed attempts earlier in the day.

t: StatBar Adds Local Weather and Fuller Mac Readouts
s: The Mac menu bar monitor can now show the local weather, details about your Mac, and fuller battery, graphics and network readouts.

t: The SnapDog Ad Gets a Voiceover and a 16.5-Second Cut
s: The SnapDog advert was re-cut to sixteen and a half seconds, given a spoken voiceover and music, and re-rendered.

t: Prism Shift's Chain Payoff Is Rebuilt From Feedback
s: The crystal game's chain payoff was rebuilt through player feedback, and it now runs on both televisions in the house.

t: QixForge Arrives on Apple TV With a Hands-On Tutorial
s: The game now runs on Apple TV, steered with the box's small remote, and new players get a hands-on tutorial.

t: Career Plan Builder Added and an Exposed Key Removed
s: The security-training site got a ninety-day career plan builder, and an exposed email-service key was removed from its public code.

t: Remnant Academy Software Goes Under Private Version Control
s: The paid training service's software and two private business documents were placed under private version control for the first time.

t: Remnant Security Course Materials Get a Canonical Home
s: The course materials behind the training business, lessons, labs and assessments, were placed under version control as the canonical source.

t: AdGenerator Renders a First SnapDog Promo Video
s: A first finished promo video for SnapDog was assembled and rendered, in both widescreen and phone-shaped versions.

t: The Red Button Now Powers the Hisense TV On and Off
s: The television's dead power button was worked around by making the red button on the remote switch the set on and off.

t: Clicking a Download Link Now Reaches My File Server
s: Clicking a download link on any of my Macs can now hand it straight to the file server's download manager.

t: Prism Shift Chain Reactions Get a Camera-Zoom Payoff
s: Chain reactions now trigger a big camera-zoom flourish, blocks pulse softly to the music, and each level's scenery lasts across several stages.

t: QixForge Gains a Hundred Songs, One Per Level
s: The game gained a hundred songs, one per level, and its animated backdrops now stay off the part of the screen where you play.

t: Getting Control Back of My Hisense TV
s: A television that had been crawling for three days turned out to be hung on a USB stick it had half-swallowed, and a second ghost drive nobody knew was there was blocking every app install.

t: Fixing a Slow Hisense TV With a Broken USB Drive
s: A slow television with a broken USB drive was diagnosed and repaired, and it now runs noticeably more smoothly.

t: Prism Shift Gets New Music for All Fifteen Levels
s: All fifteen levels now play brand-new music made on the home computer, and the game was installed on a real phone.

t: Backup Scripts Now Survive a Stuck Network Drive
s: The scripts that back up my projects and report on my Macs now survive a stuck network drive and a one-off failed copy.

t: Prism Shift Starts Relaxed and Adds Color-Vision Shapes
s: Relaxed became the starting pace for new players, and color-vision options now mark crystals with shapes as well as colors.

t: QixForge Moves to Your Beat and Adds Color-Vision Modes
s: The game now plays music and visuals in time with your moves, and offers nine color-vision settings so key things are never told apart by color alone.

t: Insider Threat Tool Compiles Again After a Year
s: A website for rating how ready an organisation is for insider threats compiles again for the first time in over a year.

t: My Skill-Sync Tool Stops Treating Backups as Skills
s: The tool that keeps Claude's skills in step across three Macs stopped treating its own backups as skills.

t: Prism Shift's Fifteen Levels Get Their Own Music
s: All fifteen levels now have their own music, backdrops and layouts, and the music slides from one level into the next without stopping play.

t: QixForge Levels Get Hand-Built Obstacles and a Pace Choice
s: Every level got hand-built obstacles to claim around, and a slower or faster game pace can now be chosen in the options.

t: SecureWatch Sheds Nearly 15,000 Leftover Build Files
s: The code history was cleared of nearly fifteen thousand leftover build files that were clogging every status check.

t: Prism Shift Passes Every Walkthrough on a Small Phone
s: Every scripted walkthrough of the whole game now passes on a small phone screen, three days before its planned release.

t: QixForge's Hardest Level Becomes Finishable
s: The game's hardest level became finishable for ordinary players, and everything was fitted to the phone screen for release.

t: CyberSim 1.1.0 Gets Its App Store Page and Paperwork
s: CyberSim got its App Store page written and its release paperwork set up, so version 1.1.0 can be sent to Apple.

t: Civic Fortune 2026: Three Ways to Win Now Work
s: Three of the game's five ways to win could never be won; they now can, and a run saves itself so you can quit and come back.

t: SnapDog's Recording Focus Fix Is Still Unfinished
s: The recording focus fix is still unfinished, and the product site gained new pictures of the order page.

t: A Bot Play-Tested All 100 QixForge Levels
s: All 100 levels were play-tested by a bot and rebalanced, and the game gained story scenes and per-sector music.

t: SnapDog Fixes Flipped Arrows and Misplaced Click Rings
s: Arrows drawn leftward no longer flip, new captures open clean, and click rings in recordings land on the click.

t: SnapDog Stops Stealing Focus When Recording Starts
s: Starting a screen recording no longer leaves SnapDog in front, so your first click lands in the app you are recording.

t: Lectern Can Now Find and Download Local AI Models
s: Lectern can now find and download local AI models inside the app, and the main screens were reworked.

t: QixForge Now Explains Why You Lost a Life
s: QixForge now explains why you lost a life, plays properly sideways, and starts on a dark screen.

t: BookForge Stops Claiming a Book Has No Chapters
s: The BookForge Mac app got a consistent look and stopped claiming a book had no chapters while it loaded.

t: StatBar's Release Build Stops Hanging on Apple's Check
s: Building a release of the app no longer hangs forever waiting on Apple's security check.
